cands.name: Hazel Floyd

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 38 in 2026, including a February 2026 special election. Graduated from the University of Alabama with a political science and philosophy degree. Says she lobbied in Montgomery as a student and spent a summer learning from the Chamber of Commerce. Has not held public office.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from Tabitha's List (Candidates You Can Trust) and Unburdening The Ballot (Voting Made Easy), both Sway voting groups, in the special election.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Floyd was born or when she began living in Alabama. Her work history outside school and campaigning is not documented. Her claim of lobbying for HB152 comes only from her own site and was not checked against legislative records. We found no sponsored bills, official actions or filings by her, since she has never held office. Her campaign pillars cover public school funding, rural economic development, farmers and small businesses. She does not state positions on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth limits, immigration, campaign money, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no documented land-use or development stances, controversies, or foreign ties.

cands.name: Kristin Nelson

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House for District 38 since February 2026, elected in a special election after Debbie Wood resigned. Former 3rd-grade teacher and seven-year City of Valley administrative employee. Homeschooling mother, part-time at Harris Gray LLC, and chair of the Chambers County Republican Party.
cands.gaps: We could not find where or when she was born, or when she might have moved within Alabama. We found no documented positions or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, school vouchers or teacher pay. Her Ballotpedia sponsored-legislation list was empty on the page we read, and the full policy page on her campaign site was not available. We found no notable endorsements, no controversies and no foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 90: She describes herself as a lifelong Chambers County resident raised there by her parents, but her birthplace is not stated in the pages reviewed. · Money: 14% of money from District 38 ZIP codes

qual.background: Seven years in administration for the City of Valley, three years as a 3rd-grade teacher at Lanett City Schools, and part-time work at Harris Gray LLC. She has held the District 38 House seat since February 2026.
qual.why: Her work history includes local government administration and teaching, which fits the middle range. Her legislative service is only a few months and no law, policy or budget career is documented. Party chairmanship and civic board roles are not counted.
